geo_basis: Bulgarian government (Sofia); the affected agencies are not named
title: Bulgaria says hackers had access to government networks for about five years
date_note: Date of the government announcement; the access began in 2021.
summary: Bulgaria's digital minister Ivan Vassilev said that since 2021 more than 130 GB, or 62 million pages, of documents had been downloaded from state networks. Per Reuters, several international hacking groups are believed responsible, with no conclusive foreign-government link; access was cut, malware removed. On 5 August, BTA reported the ministry had found unauthorised access to some administrative networks via a new national cybersecurity system. No evidence so far of compromised personal data.
plain: Bulgaria says unidentified hackers sat inside government networks for about five years and copied a very large volume of state documents. Access has been cut off.
exec: A multi-year, undetected intrusion into a national government shows how long attackers can stay hidden without central monitoring.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Government and critical-sector defenders should review document-exchange systems for long-dwell access and centralise monitoring.

sources.name: BTA (Bulgarian News Agency), 5 Aug 2026, relaying the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation's press service

validation.note: Two independent publishers (Samanyolu Haber, citing DW Türkçe; Europa FM, citing Novinite) report the minister's announcement. Detection date differs (June 23 vs August 2026) and Europa FM gives the volume in gigabits; the DW-based report says GB, so GB is used. The DW original and a government statement were not read. Follow-up 2026-11-20T12:49:50Z: Reuters (via The Star, read) gives GB (not gigabits), 62 million pages, since 2021, prosecutors notified, several international hacking groups believed responsible with no conclusive link to a foreign government; no actor named. Follow-up 2026-11-22T18:20:02Z: BTA (5 Aug, read in full) relays the ministry press service: unauthorised access to some administrative networks detected during work on the new national cybersecurity system, activity may have continued for years; no volume, start date or actor given. This supports the August detection date.

review.note: Compared with Reuters via The Star (read): 18 Nov announcement, 130 GB / 62M pages, since 2021, several groups, no conclusive foreign-government link, no personal-data evidence, access cut, malware removed
